regulation_name: Clean Water Act, Title 40 CFR Part 122 (NPDES Permitting) and Part 412 (Effluent Guidelines for CAFOs)

requirements.requirement_text: The requirements for concentrated animal feeding operations are described in Sec. 122.23(d).
requirements.plain_language_summary: Rules for Concentrated Animal Feeding Operations (CAFOs) about needing a permit are found in section 122.23(d).

requirements.requirement_text: A nutrient management plan that at a minimum satisfies the requirements specified in Sec. 122.42(e), including, for all CAFOs subject to 40 CFR part 412, subpart C or subpart D, the requirements of 40 CFR 412.4(c), as applicable.
requirements.plain_language_summary: When applying for an individual permit or submitting a notice of intent for a general permit, you must include a nutrient management plan (NMP). This NMP must meet the basic requirements in section 122.42(e) and, if your CAFO is a large beef, dairy, veal calf, swine, or poultry operation, it must also meet the specific requirements in 40 CFR 412.4(c).

requirements.requirement_text: Once an animal feeding operation is defined as a CAFO for at least one type of animal, the NPDES requirements for CAFOs apply with respect to all animals in confinement at the operation and all manure, litter, and process wastewater generated by those animals or the production of those animals, regardless of the type of animal.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your farm is classified as a CAFO for any type of animal, then all NPDES permit rules for CAFOs apply to all animals kept in confinement on your farm, and to all manure, litter, and wastewater produced by those animals, no matter what kind of animal they are.

requirements.requirement_text: The owner or operator of a CAFO must seek coverage under an NPDES permit if the CAFO discharges or proposes to discharge. A CAFO proposes to discharge if it is designed, constructed, operated, or maintained such that a discharge will occur. Specifically, the CAFO owner or operator must either apply for an individual NPDES permit or submit a notice of intent for coverage under an NPDES general permit. If the Director has not made a general permit available to the CAFO, the CAFO owner or operator must submit an application for an individual permit to the Director.
requirements.plain_language_summary: You must get an NPDES permit if your CAFO releases pollutants into U.S. waters, or if it is built, run, or kept in a way that means a release will happen. This means you need to apply for either an individual permit or a general permit. If a general permit isn't available, you must apply for an individual permit.
requirements.penalty_info: Discharging without a permit is a violation of CWA section 301(a). If it is determined that the CAFO proposed to discharge prior to the discharge, it is also in violation of the duty to apply under 40 CFR 122.23(d)(1).

requirements.requirement_text: An application for an individual permit must include the information specified in Sec. 122.21. A notice of intent for a general permit must include the information specified in Sec. Sec. 122.21 and 122.28.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you apply for an individual permit, you must provide all the information listed in section 122.21. If you submit a notice of intent for a general permit, you must provide the information listed in sections 122.21 and 122.28.

requirements.requirement_text: For unpermitted Large CAFOs, a precipitation-related discharge of manure, litter, or process wastewater from land areas under the control of a CAFO shall be considered an agricultural stormwater discharge only where the manure, litter, or process wastewater has been land applied in accordance with site-specific nutrient management practices that ensure appropriate agricultural utilization of the nutrients in the manure, litter, or process wastewater, as specified in Sec. 122.42(e)(1)(vi) through (ix).
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your Large CAFO doesn't have a permit, any rain-related runoff of manure, litter, or wastewater from your land application areas is only considered exempt 'agricultural stormwater' if you applied these materials following specific nutrient management practices. These practices must ensure the nutrients are used properly by crops, as detailed in section 122.42(e)(1)(vi) through (ix).
requirements.penalty_info: If these conditions are not met, the discharge is considered an unpermitted point source discharge, which is a violation of CWA section 301(a).

requirements.requirement_text: Unpermitted Large CAFOs must maintain documentation specified in Sec. 122.42(e)(1)(ix) either on site or at a nearby office, or otherwise make such documentation readily available to the Director or Regional Administrator upon request.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your Large CAFO doesn't have a permit, you must keep records (as described in section 122.42(e)(1)(ix)) either at your farm, a nearby office, or readily accessible to the permitting authority if they ask for it. This documentation proves your land application practices qualify for the agricultural stormwater exemption.

requirements.requirement_text: Any CAFO that is required to seek permit coverage under paragraph (d)(1) of this section must seek coverage when the CAFO proposes to discharge, unless a later deadline is specified below.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your CAFO is required to get a permit because it discharges or is set up to discharge, you must apply for that permit as soon as you plan to discharge, unless a specific later date is given in the rules below.
requirements.penalty_info: Discharging without a permit is a violation of CWA section 301(a). If it is determined that the CAFO proposed to discharge prior to the discharge, it is also in violation of the duty to apply under 40 CFR 122.23(d)(1) and (f).

requirements.requirement_text: For operations defined as CAFOs under regulations that were in effect prior to April 14, 2003, the owner or operator must have or seek to obtain coverage under an NPDES permit as of April 14, 2003, and comply with all applicable NPDES requirements, including the duty to maintain permit coverage in accordance with paragraph (g) of this section.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your farm was already considered a CAFO before April 14, 2003, you must have or apply for an NPDES permit by that date and follow all permit rules, including keeping your permit active.

requirements.requirement_text: For all operations defined as CAFOs as of April 14, 2003, that were not defined as CAFOs prior to that date, the owner or operator of the CAFO must seek to obtain coverage under an NPDES permit by February 27, 2009.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your farm was classified as a CAFO on April 14, 2003, but wasn't before that date, you must apply for an NPDES permit by February 27, 2009.

requirements.requirement_text: For newly constructed operations not subject to effluent limitations guidelines, 180 days prior to the time CAFO commences operation.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you are building a new CAFO that isn't subject to specific effluent guidelines, you must apply for an NPDES permit 180 days before you start operating.

requirements.requirement_text: For other operations (e.g., resulting from an increase in the number of animals), as soon as possible, but no later than 90 days after becoming defined as a CAFO.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your farm becomes a CAFO for the first time after April 14, 2003, due to changes like increasing animal numbers, you must apply for an NPDES permit as soon as possible, but no later than 90 days after becoming a CAFO.
requirements.deadline: 90 days after becoming defined as a CAFO

requirements.requirement_text: If an operational change that makes the operation a CAFO would not have made it a CAFO prior to April 14, 2003, the operation has until February 27, 2009, or 90 days after becoming defined as a CAFO, whichever is later.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your farm becomes a CAFO due to an operational change that wouldn't have made it a CAFO before April 14, 2003, you must apply for an NPDES permit by February 27, 2009, or 90 days after becoming a CAFO, whichever date is later.
requirements.deadline: February 27, 2009, or 90 days after becoming defined as a CAFO, whichever is later

requirements.requirement_text: The owner or operator of a new source must seek to obtain coverage under a permit at least 180 days prior to the time that the CAFO commences operation.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you are building a new CAFO (a 'new source'), you must apply for an NPDES permit at least 180 days before you start operating.

requirements.requirement_text: For operations designated as a CAFO in accordance with paragraph (c) of this section, the owner or operator must seek to obtain coverage under a permit no later than 90 days after receiving notice of the designation.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your farm is officially designated as a CAFO by the permitting authority, you must apply for an NPDES permit no later than 90 days after you receive that notice.
requirements.deadline: 90 days after receiving notice of designation

requirements.requirement_text: No later than 180 days before the expiration of the permit, or as provided by the Director, any permitted CAFO must submit an application to renew its permit, in accordance with Sec. 122.21(d), unless the CAFO will not discharge or propose to discharge upon expiration of the permit.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your CAFO has a permit, you must apply to renew it at least 180 days before it expires, or by a date set by the Director. You don't need to renew if your CAFO will no longer discharge or be set up to discharge when the permit expires.

requirements.requirement_text: CAFO owners or operators must submit a notice of intent when seeking authorization to discharge under a general permit in accordance with Sec. 122.28(b).
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you want to operate your CAFO under a general permit, you must submit a notice of intent (NOI) as required by section 122.28(b).

requirements.requirement_text: The Director must review notices of intent submitted by CAFO owners or operators to ensure that the notice of intent includes the information required by Sec. 122.21(i)(1), including a nutrient management plan that meets the requirements of Sec. 122.42(e) and applicable effluent limitations and standards, including those specified in 40 CFR part 412.
requirements.plain_language_summary: The permitting authority (Director) must check your notice of intent (NOI) to make sure it has all the information required by section 122.21(i)(1), including a nutrient management plan (NMP) that meets the rules in section 122.42(e) and any other relevant discharge limits, especially those in 40 CFR part 412.

requirements.requirement_text: When additional information is necessary to complete the notice of intent or clarify, modify, or supplement previously submitted material, the Director may request such information from the owner or operator.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If the permitting authority (Director) needs more information to complete your notice of intent (NOI) or to clarify, change, or add to what you've already submitted, they can ask you for it.

requirements.requirement_text: If the Director makes a preliminary determination that the notice of intent meets the requirements of Sec. Sec. 122.21(i)(1) and 122.42(e), the Director must notify the public of the Director's proposal to grant coverage under the permit to the CAFO and make available for public review and comment the notice of intent submitted by the CAFO, including the CAFO's nutrient management plan, and the draft terms of the nutrient management plan to be incorporated into the permit.
requirements.plain_language_summary: Once the permitting authority (Director) decides your notice of intent (NOI) and nutrient management plan (NMP) meet the initial requirements, they must tell the public that they plan to give your CAFO permit coverage. They must also make your NOI, NMP, and the proposed NMP terms for your permit available for public review and comments.

requirements.requirement_text: The process for submitting public comments and hearing requests, and the hearing process if a request for a hearing is granted, must follow the procedures applicable to draft permits set forth in 40 CFR 124.11 through 124.13.
requirements.plain_language_summary: The rules for how the public can submit comments, ask for a hearing, and how a hearing is conducted for your CAFO's general permit application are the same as those for draft permits, found in 40 CFR 124.11 through 124.13.

requirements.requirement_text: The Director may establish, either by regulation or in the general permit, an appropriate period of time for the public to comment and request a hearing that differs from the time period specified in 40 CFR 124.10.
requirements.plain_language_summary: The permitting authority (Director) can set a specific timeframe for public comments and hearing requests, either in a regulation or in the general permit itself. This timeframe might be different from the usual 30-day period mentioned in 40 CFR 124.10.

requirements.requirement_text: The Director must respond to significant comments received during the comment period, as provided in 40 CFR 124.17, and, if necessary, require the CAFO owner or operator to revise the nutrient management plan in order to be granted permit coverage.
requirements.plain_language_summary: The permitting authority (Director) must respond to important comments received during the public comment period, as outlined in 40 CFR 124.17. If needed, they must also require you to update your nutrient management plan (NMP) before you can get permit coverage.

requirements.requirement_text: When the Director authorizes coverage for the CAFO owner or operator under the general permit, the terms of the nutrient management plan shall become incorporated as terms and conditions of the permit for the CAFO. The Director shall notify the CAFO owner or operator and inform the public that coverage has been authorized and of the terms of the nutrient management plan incorporated as terms and conditions of the permit applicable to the CAFO.
requirements.plain_language_summary: Once the permitting authority (Director) approves your CAFO for a general permit, the specific details of your nutrient management plan (NMP) become official, enforceable parts of your permit. The Director must then tell you and the public that your permit coverage is approved and what NMP terms are included in your permit.

requirements.requirement_text: For EPA-issued permits only. The Regional Administrator shall notify each person who has submitted written comments on the proposal to grant coverage and the draft terms of the nutrient management plan or requested notice of the final permit decision. Such notification shall include notice that coverage has been authorized and of the terms of the nutrient management plan incorporated as terms and conditions of the permit applicable to the CAFO.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If EPA issues your permit, the Regional Administrator must notify everyone who commented on your permit proposal or asked for notice of the final decision. This notice will confirm that your permit coverage is approved and list the nutrient management plan (NMP) terms that are now part of your permit.

requirements.requirement_text: The owner or operator of a CAFO that meets the eligibility criteria in paragraph (i)(2) of this section may certify to the Director that the CAFO does not discharge or propose to discharge. A CAFO owner or operator who certifies that the CAFO does not discharge or propose to discharge is not required to seek coverage under an NPDES permit pursuant to paragraph (d)(1) of this section, provided that the CAFO is designed, constructed, operated, and maintained in accordance with the requirements of paragraphs (i)(2) and (3) of this section, and subject to the limitations in paragraph (i)(4) of this section.
requirements.plain_language_summary: You can voluntarily tell the permitting authority (Director) that your CAFO doesn't discharge or isn't set up to discharge, if you meet certain eligibility rules. If you do this and follow the rules for design, construction, operation, and maintenance, you won't need an NPDES permit.
requirements.penalty_info: Discharging without a permit is a violation of CWA section 301(a). If the CAFO is not designed, constructed, operated, and maintained in accordance with the certification requirements, the certification is invalid, and the CAFO may be in violation of the duty to apply if it discharges or proposes to discharge.

requirements.requirement_text: In order to certify that a CAFO does not discharge or propose to discharge, the owner or operator of a CAFO must document, based on an objective assessment of the conditions at the CAFO, that the CAFO is designed, constructed, operated, and maintained in a manner such that the CAFO will not discharge, as follows:
requirements.plain_language_summary: To certify that your CAFO doesn't discharge or isn't set up to discharge, you must objectively prove through documentation that your CAFO's design, construction, operation, and maintenance prevent any discharges.

requirements.requirement_text: Any open manure storage structures are designed, constructed, operated, and maintained to achieve no discharge based on a technical evaluation in accordance with the elements of the technical evaluation set forth in 40 CFR 412.46(a)(1)(i) through (viii);
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your CAFO has open manure storage, you must prove through a technical evaluation (following the steps in 40 CFR 412.46(a)(1)(i) through (viii)) that these structures are designed, built, run, and maintained to prevent any discharges.

requirements.requirement_text: Any part of the CAFO's production area that is not addressed by paragraph (i)(2)(i)(A) of this section is designed, constructed, operated, and maintained such that there will be no discharge of manure, litter, or process wastewater; and
requirements.plain_language_summary: Any part of your CAFO's production area not covered by the open manure storage rules must also be designed, built, run, and maintained to prevent any discharge of manure, litter, or wastewater.

requirements.requirement_text: The CAFO implements the additional measures set forth in 40 CFR 412.37(a) and (b);
requirements.plain_language_summary: Your CAFO must follow the extra rules for operation and maintenance found in 40 CFR 412.37(a) and (b).

requirements.requirement_text: The CAFO has developed and is implementing an up-to-date nutrient management plan to ensure no discharge from the CAFO, including from all land application areas under the control of the CAFO, that addresses, at a minimum, the following: (A) The elements of Sec. 122.42(e)(1)(i) through (ix) and 40 CFR 412.37(c); and (B) All site-specific operation and maintenance practices necessary to ensure no discharge, including any practices or conditions established by a technical evaluation pursuant to paragraph (i)(2)(i)(A) of this section; and
requirements.plain_language_summary: Your CAFO must have and follow a current nutrient management plan (NMP) that prevents any discharges from your farm, including from land where you apply manure. This NMP must cover at least the items in sections 122.42(e)(1)(i) through (ix) and 40 CFR 412.37(c), plus any specific operation and maintenance practices needed to prevent discharges, especially those identified in the technical evaluation for open manure storage.

requirements.requirement_text: The CAFO must maintain documentation required by this paragraph either on site or at a nearby office, or otherwise make such documentation readily available to the Director or Regional Administrator upon request.
requirements.plain_language_summary: You must keep all required documentation for your certification either at your farm, a nearby office, or readily accessible to the permitting authority if they ask for it.

requirements.requirement_text: In order to certify that a CAFO does not discharge or propose to discharge, the CAFO owner or operator must complete and submit to the Director, by certified mail or equivalent method of documentation, a certification that includes, at a minimum, the following information: (i) The legal name, address and phone number of the CAFO owner or operator (see Sec. 122.21(b)); (ii) The CAFO name and address, the county name and the latitude and longitude where the CAFO is located; (iii) A statement that describes the basis for the CAFO's certification that it satisfies the eligibility requirements identified in paragraph (i)(2) of this section; and (iv) The following certification statement: 'I certify under penalty of law that I am the owner or operator of a concentrated animal feeding operation (CAFO), identified as [Name of CAFO], and that said CAFO meets the requirements of 40 CFR 122.23(i). I have read and understand the eligibility requirements of 40 CFR 122.23(i)(2) for certifying that a CAFO does not discharge or propose to discharge and further certify that this CAFO satisfies the eligibility requirements. As part of this certification, I am including the information required by 40 CFR 122.23(i)(3). I also understand the conditions set forth in 40 CFR 122.23(i)(4), (5) and (6) regarding loss and withdrawal of certification. I certify under penalty of law that this document and all other documents required for this certification were prepared under my direction or supervision and that qualified personnel properly gathered and evaluated the information submitted. Based upon my inquiry of the person or persons directly involved in gathering and evaluating the information, the information submitted is to the best of my knowledge and belief true, accurate and complete. I am aware there are significant penalties for submitting false information, including the possibility of fine and imprisonment for knowing violations.'; and (v) The certification must be signed in accordance with the signatory requirements of 40 CFR 122.22.
requirements.plain_language_summary: To certify your CAFO doesn't discharge, you must fill out and send a certification form to the permitting authority (Director) using certified mail or a similar tracking method. This form must include your legal name, address, phone number, CAFO name, location (including latitude and longitude), a statement explaining how your CAFO meets the eligibility rules, a specific certification statement, and your official signature as required by 40 CFR 122.22.
requirements.penalty_info: Significant penalties for submitting false information, including fine and imprisonment for knowing violations.

requirements.requirement_text: A certification that meets the requirements of paragraphs (i)(2) and (i)(3) of this section shall become effective on the date it is submitted, unless the Director establishes an effective date of up to 30 days after the date of submission. Certification will remain in effect for five years or until the certification is no longer valid or is withdrawn, whichever occurs first. A certification is no longer valid when a discharge has occurred or when the CAFO ceases to meet the eligibility criteria in paragraph (i)(2) of this section.
requirements.plain_language_summary: Your certification becomes active on the day you submit it, unless the Director sets a later date (up to 30 days after submission). It lasts for five years, or until it's no longer valid (meaning a discharge happened or you no longer meet the eligibility rules) or you withdraw it, whichever comes first.
requirements.penalty_info: If a certified CAFO discharges, it is a violation of CWA section 301(a). If the CAFO ceases to meet eligibility criteria, the certification is no longer valid.

requirements.requirement_text: At any time, a CAFO may withdraw its certification by notifying the Director by certified mail or equivalent method of documentation. A certification is withdrawn on the date the notification is submitted to the Director. The CAFO does not need to specify any reason for the withdrawal in its notification to the Director.
requirements.plain_language_summary: You can withdraw your certification at any time by sending a notice to the Director via certified mail or a similar tracked method. The withdrawal is effective on the date you send the notice, and you don't need to explain why you're withdrawing it.

requirements.requirement_text: If a certification becomes invalid in accordance with paragraph (i)(4) of this section, the CAFO must withdraw its certification within three days of the date on which the CAFO becomes aware that the certification is invalid. Once a CAFO's certification is no longer valid, the CAFO is subject to the requirement in paragraph (d)(1) of this section to seek permit coverage if it discharges or proposes to discharge.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your certification becomes invalid (e.g., due to a discharge or not meeting eligibility rules), you must withdraw it within three days of realizing it's invalid. After withdrawal, if your CAFO discharges or is set up to discharge, you must apply for an NPDES permit.
requirements.deadline: 3 days of becoming aware certification is invalid
requirements.penalty_info: Failure to withdraw an invalid certification is a violation of this regulatory requirement.

requirements.requirement_text: A previously certified CAFO that does not discharge or propose to discharge may recertify in accordance with paragraph (i) of this section, except that where the CAFO has discharged, the CAFO may only recertify if the following additional conditions are met:
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your CAFO was previously certified and doesn't discharge or isn't set up to discharge, you can recertify. However, if your CAFO has had a discharge, you can only recertify if you meet specific extra conditions.

requirements.requirement_text: The CAFO had a valid certification at the time of the discharge;
requirements.plain_language_summary: To recertify after a discharge, your CAFO must have had a valid certification when the discharge happened.

requirements.requirement_text: The owner or operator satisfies the eligibility criteria of paragraph (i)(2) of this section, including any necessary modifications to the CAFO's design, construction, operation, and/or maintenance to permanently address the cause of the discharge and ensure that no discharge from this cause occurs in the future;
requirements.plain_language_summary: To recertify after a discharge, you must meet all the original eligibility rules, and you must have made any needed changes to your CAFO's design, construction, operation, or maintenance to permanently fix what caused the discharge and prevent it from happening again.

requirements.requirement_text: The CAFO has not previously recertified after a discharge from the same cause;
requirements.plain_language_summary: To recertify after a discharge, your CAFO must not have already recertified for a discharge caused by the same issue before.

requirements.requirement_text: The owner or operator submits to the Director for review the following documentation: a description of the discharge, including the date, time, cause, duration, and approximate volume of the discharge, and a detailed explanation of the steps taken by the CAFO to permanently address the cause of the discharge in addition to submitting a certification in accordance with paragraph (i)(3) of this section; and
requirements.plain_language_summary: To recertify after a discharge, you must submit to the Director for review a description of the discharge (date, time, cause, length, and estimated amount) and a detailed explanation of how you permanently fixed the cause. This is in addition to submitting the regular certification form.

requirements.requirement_text: Notwithstanding paragraph (i)(4) of this section, a recertification that meets the requirements of paragraphs (i)(6)(iii) and (i)(6)(iv) of this section shall only become effective 30 days from the date of submission of the recertification documentation.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you recertify after a discharge and meet the specific conditions for recertification, your new certification will only become active 30 days after you submit all the required recertification documents.

requirements.requirement_text: An unpermitted CAFO certified in accordance with paragraph (i) of this section is presumed not to propose to discharge. If such a CAFO does discharge, it is not in violation of the requirement that CAFOs that propose to discharge seek permit coverage pursuant to paragraphs (d)(1) and (f) of this section, with respect to that discharge. In all instances, the discharge of a pollutant without a permit is a violation of the Clean Water Act section 301(a) prohibition against unauthorized discharges from point sources.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your unpermitted CAFO has a valid certification, it's assumed you don't intend to discharge. If a discharge accidentally happens, you won't be penalized for failing to apply for a permit beforehand. However, any discharge without a permit is still a violation of the Clean Water Act.
requirements.penalty_info: Discharge of a pollutant without a permit is a violation of CWA section 301(a).

requirements.requirement_text: In any enforcement proceeding for failure to seek permit coverage under paragraphs (d)(1) or (f) of this section that is related to a discharge from an unpermitted CAFO, the burden is on the CAFO to establish that it did not propose to discharge prior to the discharge when the CAFO either did not submit certification documentation as provided in paragraph (i)(3) or (i)(6)(iv) of this section within at least five years prior to the discharge, or withdrew its certification in accordance with paragraph (i)(5) of this section. Design, construction, operation, and maintenance in accordance with the criteria of paragraph (i)(2) of this section satisfies this burden.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your unpermitted CAFO discharges and you haven't submitted a valid certification in the last five years, or you withdrew your certification, it's your responsibility to prove that you weren't planning to discharge before the event. You can meet this by showing your CAFO's design, construction, operation, and maintenance followed the certification eligibility rules.
requirements.penalty_info: Failure to establish that the CAFO did not propose to discharge prior to the discharge could result in enforcement for failure to seek permit coverage.

requirements.requirement_text: A CAFO owner or operator may be authorized to discharge under a general permit only in accordance with the process described in Sec. 122.23(h).
requirements.plain_language_summary: You can only get approval to discharge under a general permit if you follow the specific application and review process outlined in section 122.23(h).

requirements.requirement_text: Any permit issued to a CAFO must include the requirements in paragraphs (e)(1) through (e)(6) of this section.
requirements.plain_language_summary: Every permit issued to a CAFO must contain all the rules and conditions listed in paragraphs (e)(1) through (e)(6) of this section.

requirements.requirement_text: Any permit issued to a CAFO must include a requirement to implement a nutrient management plan that, at a minimum, contains best management practices necessary to meet the requirements of this paragraph and applicable effluent limitations and standards, including those specified in 40 CFR part 412. The nutrient management plan must, to the extent applicable: [followed by (i)-(ix)]
requirements.plain_language_summary: Your CAFO permit must require you to follow a nutrient management plan (NMP). This NMP must, at a minimum, include best management practices (BMPs) needed to meet the rules in this section and any other discharge limits, especially those in 40 CFR part 412. The NMP must cover all applicable items from (i) through (ix).

requirements.requirement_text: The actual crop(s) planted and actual yield(s) for each field, the actual nitrogen and phosphorus content of the manure, litter, and process wastewater, the results of calculations conducted in accordance with paragraphs (e)(5)(i)(B) and (e)(5)(ii)(D) of this section, and the amount of manure, litter, and process wastewater applied to each field during the previous 12 months; and, for any CAFO that implements a nutrient management plan that addresses rates of application in accordance with paragraph (e)(5)(ii) of this section, the results of any soil testing for nitrogen and phosphorus taken during the preceding 12 months, the data used in calculations conducted in accordance with paragraph (e)(5)(ii)(D) of this section, and the amount of any supplemental fertilizer applied during the previous 12 months.
requirements.plain_language_summary: Your annual report must include: the actual crops planted and their yields for each field, the actual nitrogen and phosphorus levels in your manure/litter/wastewater, the results of specific calculations (from sections (e)(5)(i)(B) and (e)(5)(ii)(D)), and the amount of manure/litter/wastewater applied to each field in the last year. If you use the 'narrative rate approach' for your NMP, you must also report soil test results for nitrogen and phosphorus from the last year, the data used in your calculations (from (e)(5)(ii)(D)), and any extra fertilizer applied.

requirements.requirement_text: Any permit issued to a CAFO must require compliance with the terms of the CAFO's site-specific nutrient management plan. The terms of the nutrient management plan are the information, protocols, best management practices, and other conditions in the nutrient management plan determined by the Director to be necessary to meet the requirements of paragraph (e)(1) of this section. The terms of the nutrient management plan, with respect to protocols for land application of manure, litter, or process wastewater required by paragraph (e)(1)(viii) of this section and, as applicable, 40 CFR 412.4(c), must include the fields available for land application; field-specific rates of application properly developed, as specified in paragraphs (e)(5)(i) through (ii) of this section, to ensure appropriate agricultural utilization of the nutrients in the manure, litter, or process wastewater; and any timing limitations identified in the nutrient management plan concerning land application on the fields available for land application. The terms must address rates of application using one of the following two approaches, unless the Director specifies that only one of these approaches may be used:
requirements.plain_language_summary: Your CAFO permit must require you to follow the specific 'terms' of your nutrient management plan (NMP). These terms include the information, procedures, best practices, and other conditions that the Director decides are necessary to meet the NMP rules. For land application, these terms must include the fields you can use, the specific application rates for each field (developed using either the 'linear' or 'narrative rate' approach), and any time limits for applying manure to those fields. You can choose either the linear or narrative rate approach, unless the Director tells you to use only one.

requirements.requirement_text: The terms include maximum application rates from manure, litter, and process wastewater for each year of permit coverage, for each crop identified in the nutrient management plan, in chemical forms determined to be acceptable to the Director, in pounds per acre, per year, for each field to be used for land application, and certain factors necessary to determine such rates. At a minimum, the factors that are terms must include: The outcome of the field-specific assessment of the potential for nitrogen and phosphorus transport from each field; the crops to be planted in each field or any other uses of a field such as pasture or fallow fields; the realistic yield goal for each crop or use identified for each field; the nitrogen and phosphorus recommendations from sources specified by the Director for each crop or use identified for each field; credits for all nitrogen in the field that will be plant available; consideration of multi-year phosphorus application; and accounting for all other additions of plant available nitrogen and phosphorus to the field. In addition, the terms include the form and source of manure, litter, and process wastewater to be land-applied; the timing and method of land application; and the methodology by which the nutrient management plan accounts for the amount of nitrogen and phosphorus in the manure, litter, and process wastewater to be applied.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you choose the 'linear approach' for your NMP, your permit terms must include the maximum amounts of nitrogen and phosphorus (in pounds per acre per year) from manure, litter, and wastewater that you can apply to each field for each crop, for every year of your permit. These terms also include: the risk assessment for nutrient movement from each field, the specific crops or uses for each field, realistic yield goals, nitrogen and phosphorus recommendations from approved sources, credits for plant-available nitrogen already in the soil, plans for multi-year phosphorus application, accounting for other nutrient additions, the type and source of manure/litter/wastewater, the timing and method of application, and the method you use to calculate the nutrient content of the applied materials.

requirements.requirement_text: Large CAFOs that use this approach must calculate the maximum amount of manure, litter, and process wastewater to be land applied at least once each year using the results of the most recent representative manure, litter, and process wastewater tests for nitrogen and phosphorus taken within 12 months of the date of land application; or
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your Large CAFO uses the 'linear approach', you must calculate the maximum amount of manure, litter, and wastewater you can apply at least once a year. This calculation must use the most recent test results for nitrogen and phosphorus in your manure, litter, and wastewater, taken within 12 months before you apply it.
requirements.deadline: At least once each year, using tests taken within 12 months of land application date

requirements.requirement_text: The terms include maximum amounts of nitrogen and phosphorus derived from all sources of nutrients, for each crop identified in the nutrient management plan, in chemical forms determined to be acceptable to the Director, in pounds per acre, for each field, and certain factors necessary to determine such amounts. At a minimum, the factors that are terms must include: the outcome of the field-specific assessment of the potential for nitrogen and phosphorus transport from each field; the crops to be planted in each field or any other uses such as pasture or fallow fields (including alternative crops identified in accordance with paragraph (e)(5)(ii)(B) of this section); the realistic yield goal for each crop or use identified for each field; and the nitrogen and phosphorus recommendations from sources specified by the Director for each crop or use identified for each field. In addition, the terms include the methodology by which the nutrient management plan accounts for the following factors when calculating the amounts of manure, litter, and process wastewater to be land applied: Results of soil tests conducted in accordance with protocols identified in the nutrient management plan, as required by paragraph (e)(1)(vii) of this section; credits for all nitrogen in the field that will be plant available; the amount of nitrogen and phosphorus in the manure, litter, and process wastewater to be applied; consideration of multi-year phosphorus application; accounting for all other additions of plant available nitrogen and phosphorus to the field; the form and source of manure, litter, and process wastewater; the timing and method of land application; and volatilization of nitrogen and mineralization of organic nitrogen.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you choose the 'narrative rate approach' for your NMP, your permit terms must include the maximum total amounts of nitrogen and phosphorus (in pounds per acre) from all nutrient sources for each crop on each field. These terms also include: the risk assessment for nutrient movement from each field, the crops or uses for each field (including alternative crops), realistic yield goals, and nitrogen and phosphorus recommendations from approved sources. Crucially, the terms also include the specific method you use to calculate how much manure, litter, and wastewater to apply, taking into account: soil test results, plant-available nitrogen credits, the nutrient content of your manure/litter/wastewater, multi-year phosphorus plans, other nutrient additions, the type and source of materials, application timing and method, and nitrogen loss/conversion.

requirements.requirement_text: The terms of the nutrient management plan include alternative crops identified in the CAFO's nutrient management plan that are not in the planned crop rotation. Where a CAFO includes alternative crops in its nutrient management plan, the crops must be listed by field, in addition to the crops identified in the planned crop rotation for that field, and the nutrient management plan must include realistic crop yield goals and the nitrogen and phosphorus recommendations from sources specified by the Director for each crop. Maximum amounts of nitrogen and phosphorus from all sources of nutrients and the amounts of manure, litter, and process wastewater to be applied must be determined in accordance with the methodology described in paragraph (e)(5)(ii)(A) of this section.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you use the 'narrative rate approach', your NMP's terms must include any alternative crops you might plant, even if they're not in your main crop rotation. For each alternative crop on each field, your NMP must list realistic yield goals and nitrogen/phosphorus recommendations from approved sources. The maximum nutrient amounts and manure/litter/wastewater application amounts for these alternative crops must be calculated using the method described in section (e)(5)(ii)(A).

requirements.requirement_text: CAFOs that use this approach must calculate maximum amounts of manure, litter, and process wastewater to be land applied at least once each year using the methodology required in paragraph (e)(5)(ii)(A) of this section before land applying manure, litter, and process wastewater and must rely on the following data: (1) A field-specific determination of soil levels of nitrogen and phosphorus, including, for nitrogen, a concurrent determination of nitrogen that will be plant available consistent with the methodology required by paragraph (e)(5)(ii)(A) of this section, and for phosphorus, the results of the most recent soil test conducted in accordance with soil testing requirements approved by the Director; and (2) The results of most recent representative manure, litter, and process wastewater tests for nitrogen and phosphorus taken within 12 months of the date of land application, in order to determine the amount of nitrogen and phosphorus in the manure, litter, and process wastewater to be applied.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your CAFO uses the 'narrative rate approach', you must calculate the maximum amounts of manure, litter, and wastewater to apply at least once a year, using the method from section (e)(5)(ii)(A), before you apply it. You must use: 1) current field-specific soil tests for nitrogen (including plant-available nitrogen) and phosphorus (using the latest test results approved by the Director); and 2) the most recent tests (within 12 months of application) for nitrogen and phosphorus content in your manure, litter, and wastewater.
requirements.deadline: At least once each year before land application, using tests taken within 12 months of land application date

requirements.requirement_text: The CAFO owner or operator must provide the Director with the most current version of the CAFO's nutrient management plan and identify changes from the previous version, except that the results of calculations made in accordance with the requirements of paragraphs (e)(5)(i)(B) and (e)(5)(ii)(D) of this section are not subject to the requirements of paragraph (e)(6) of this section.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you make any changes to your nutrient management plan (NMP), you must give the Director the most current version and point out what's changed. However, the annual calculations for manure application rates (from sections (e)(5)(i)(B) and (e)(5)(ii)(D)) don't need to be submitted as NMP changes.

requirements.requirement_text: The Director must review the revised nutrient management plan to ensure that it meets the requirements of this section and applicable effluent limitations and standards, including those specified in 40 CFR part 412, and must determine whether the changes to the nutrient management plan necessitate revision to the terms of the nutrient management plan incorporated into the permit issued to the CAFO. If revision to the terms of the nutrient management plan is not necessary, the Director must notify the CAFO owner or operator and upon such notification the CAFO may implement the revised nutrient management plan. If revision to the terms of the nutrient management plan is necessary, the Director must determine whether such changes are substantial changes as described in paragraph (e)(6)(iii) of this section.
requirements.plain_language_summary: The permitting authority (Director) must review your updated nutrient management plan (NMP) to ensure it still meets all rules and discharge limits. They will decide if the changes require updating the NMP terms in your permit. If not, they'll tell you, and you can start using the revised NMP. If changes to the permit terms are needed, the Director will then decide if these are 'substantial changes' as defined in section (e)(6)(iii).

requirements.requirement_text: If the Director determines that the changes to the terms of the nutrient management plan are not substantial, the Director must make the revised nutrient management plan publicly available and include it in the permit record, revise the terms of the nutrient management plan incorporated into the permit, and notify the owner or operator and inform the public of any changes to the terms of the nutrient management plan that are incorporated into the permit.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If the Director decides your NMP changes are not 'substantial', they must make the updated NMP public, add it to your permit file, update the NMP terms in your permit, and tell you and the public about these changes.

requirements.requirement_text: If the Director determines that the changes to the terms of the nutrient management plan are substantial, the Director must notify the public and make the proposed changes and the information submitted by the CAFO owner or operator available for public review and comment. The process for public comments, hearing requests, and the hearing process if a hearing is held must follow the procedures applicable to draft permits set forth in 40 CFR 124.11 through 124.13. The Director may establish, either by regulation or in the CAFO's permit, an appropriate period of time for the public to comment and request a hearing on the proposed changes that differs from the time period specified in 40 CFR 124.10. The Director must respond to all significant comments received during the comment period as provided in 40 CFR 124.17, and require the CAFO owner or operator to further revise the nutrient management plan if necessary, in order to approve the revision to the terms of the nutrient management plan incorporated into the CAFO's permit. Once the Director incorporates the revised terms of the nutrient management plan into the permit, the Director must notify the owner or operator and inform the public of the final decision concerning revisions to the terms and conditions of the permit.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If the Director decides your NMP changes are 'substantial', they must tell the public and make your proposed changes and submitted information available for public review and comment. The rules for public comments and hearings are the same as for draft permits (40 CFR 124.11-124.13). The Director can set a different public comment period than the usual 30 days. The Director must respond to all important comments and may require you to further revise your NMP. Once the revised NMP terms are in your permit, the Director must notify you and the public of the final decision.

requirements.requirement_text: Addition of new land application areas not previously included in the CAFO's nutrient management plan. Except that if the land application area that is being added to the nutrient management plan is covered by terms of a nutrient management plan incorporated into an existing NPDES permit in accordance with the requirements of paragraph (e)(5) of this section, and the CAFO owner or operator applies manure, litter, or process wastewater on the newly added land application area in accordance with the existing field-specific permit terms applicable to the newly added land application area, such addition of new land would be a change to the new CAFO owner or operator's nutrient management plan but not a substantial change for purposes of this section;
requirements.plain_language_summary: Adding new land for manure application that wasn't in your NMP before is a 'substantial change'. However, if that new land is already covered by another existing NPDES permit's NMP terms, and you apply manure according to those existing terms, then adding that land to your NMP is not considered a substantial change.

requirements.requirement_text: Any changes to the field-specific maximum annual rates for land application, as set forth in paragraphs (e)(5)(i) of this section, and to the maximum amounts of nitrogen and phosphorus derived from all sources for each crop, as set forth in paragraph (e)(5)(ii) of this section;
requirements.plain_language_summary: Any changes to the maximum annual manure application rates for specific fields (if you use the 'linear approach') or to the maximum total nitrogen and phosphorus amounts from all sources for each crop (if you use the 'narrative rate approach') are considered 'substantial changes'.

requirements.requirement_text: Addition of any crop or other uses not included in the terms of the CAFO's nutrient management plan and corresponding field-specific rates of application expressed in accordance with paragraph (e)(5) of this section; and
requirements.plain_language_summary: Adding any new crop or other land use that wasn't already in your NMP's terms, along with its specific application rates, is considered a 'substantial change'.

requirements.requirement_text: Changes to site-specific components of the CAFO's nutrient management plan, where such changes are likely to increase the risk of nitrogen and phosphorus transport to waters of the U.S.
requirements.plain_language_summary: Any changes to specific parts of your CAFO's NMP that could increase the chance of nitrogen and phosphorus runoff into U.S. waters are considered 'substantial changes'.

requirements.requirement_text: Incorporate changes to the terms of a CAFO's nutrient management plan that have been revised in accordance with the requirements of Sec. 122.42(e)(6).
requirements.plain_language_summary: Changes to the terms of your CAFO's nutrient management plan (NMP) that follow the rules in section 122.42(e)(6) can be added to your permit as a 'minor modification'.

requirements.requirement_text: All open surface liquid impoundments must have a depth marker which clearly indicates the minimum capacity necessary to contain the runoff and direct precipitation of the 25-year, 24-hour rainfall event. In the case of new sources subject to effluent limitations established pursuant to Sec. 412.46(a)(1) of this part, all open surface manure storage structures associated with such sources must include a depth marker which clearly indicates the minimum capacity necessary to contain the maximum runoff and direct precipitation associated with the design storm used in sizing the impoundment for no discharge.
requirements.plain_language_summary: All open liquid manure storage areas must have a marker showing the minimum level needed to hold runoff and rain from a 25-year, 24-hour storm. For new CAFOs that must meet 'no discharge' rules (under section 412.46(a)(1)), their open manure storage must have a marker showing the minimum capacity needed for the design storm that ensures no discharge.

requirements.requirement_text: Any CAFO subject to this subpart may request that the Director establish NPDES permit best management practice effluent limitations designed to ensure no discharge of manure, litter, or process wastewater based upon a site-specific evaluation of the CAFO's open surface manure storage structure. The NPDES permit best management practice effluent limitations must address the CAFO's entire production area. In the case of any CAFO using an open surface manure storage structure for which the Director establishes such effluent limitations, 'no discharge of manure, litter, or process wastewater pollutants,' as used in this section, means that the storage structure is designed, operated, and maintained in accordance with best management practices established by the Director on a site-specific basis after a technical evaluation of the storage structure. The technical evaluation must address the following elements:
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your CAFO is a new source (swine, poultry, veal calf), you can ask the Director to set specific permit limits based on best management practices (BMPs) for your open manure storage. These BMPs must ensure no discharge of manure, litter, or wastewater from your entire production area. 'No discharge' means your storage is designed, run, and maintained according to BMPs set by the Director after a technical review. This review must cover specific elements:

requirements.requirement_text: Information to be used in the design of the open manure storage structure including, but not limited to, the following: minimum storage periods for rainy seasons, additional minimum capacity for chronic rainfalls, applicable technical standards that prohibit or otherwise limit land application to frozen, saturated, or snow-covered ground, planned emptying and dewatering schedules consistent with the CAFO's Nutrient Management Plan, additional storage capacity for manure intended to be transferred to another recipient at a later time, and any other factors that would affect the sizing of the open manure storage structure.
requirements.plain_language_summary: Your technical evaluation for open manure storage must include design information like: minimum storage time for rainy seasons, extra capacity for long rainfalls, rules against applying manure to frozen/wet/snowy ground, planned emptying schedules from your NMP, extra storage for manure you plan to transfer, and any other factors that impact the size of your storage.

requirements.requirement_text: The design of the open manure storage structure as determined by the most recent version of the National Resource Conservation Service's Animal Waste Management (AWM) software. CAFOs may use equivalent design software or procedures as approved by the Director.
requirements.plain_language_summary: Your open manure storage must be designed using the latest Animal Waste Management (AWM) software from the Natural Resources Conservation Service. You can use other design software or methods if the Director approves them.

requirements.requirement_text: All inputs used in the open manure storage structure design including actual climate data for the previous 30 years consisting of historical average monthly precipitation and evaporation values, the number and types of animals, anticipated animal sizes or weights, any added water and bedding, any other process wastewater, and the size and condition of outside areas exposed to rainfall and contributing runoff to the open manure storage structure.
requirements.plain_language_summary: Your design for open manure storage must include all inputs like: 30 years of historical monthly rainfall and evaporation data, the number and types of animals, their expected sizes/weights, any added water or bedding, other wastewater, and the size and condition of outdoor areas that drain into the storage.

requirements.requirement_text: The planned minimum period of storage in months including, but not limited to, the factors for designing an open manure storage structure listed in paragraph (a)(1)(i) of this section. Alternatively the CAFO may determine the minimum period of storage by specifying times the storage pond will be emptied consistent with the CAFO's Nutrient Management Plan.
requirements.plain_language_summary: Your plan must state the minimum number of months you'll store manure, considering the design factors from section (a)(1)(i). Or, you can specify when the storage pond will be emptied, as long as it matches your Nutrient Management Plan.

requirements.requirement_text: Site-specific predicted design specifications including dimensions of the storage facility, daily manure and wastewater additions, the size and characteristics of the land application areas, and the total calculated storage period in months.
requirements.plain_language_summary: Your design must include specific details for your site, such as the size of the storage facility, how much manure and wastewater is added daily, the size and features of your land application areas, and the total calculated storage time in months.

requirements.requirement_text: An evaluation of the adequacy of the designed manure storage structure using the most recent version of the Soil Plant Air Water (SPAW) Hydrology Tool. The evaluation must include all inputs to SPAW including but not limited to daily precipitation, temperature, and evaporation data for the previous 100 years, user-specified soil profiles representative of the CAFO's land application areas, planned crop rotations consistent with the CAFO's Nutrient Management Plan, and the final modeled result of no overflows from the designed open manure storage structure. For those CAFOs where 100 years of local weather data for the CAFO's location is not available, CAFOs may use a simulation with a confidence interval analysis conducted over a period of 100 years. The Director may approve equivalent evaluation and simulation procedures.
requirements.plain_language_summary: You must evaluate if your manure storage design is adequate using the latest Soil Plant Air Water (SPAW) Hydrology Tool. This evaluation must include all data for SPAW, such as 100 years of daily rainfall, temperature, and evaporation data, soil types for your application areas, planned crop rotations from your NMP, and show that your open storage will not overflow. If 100 years of local weather data isn't available, you can use a 100-year simulation with a confidence analysis. The Director can approve other equivalent evaluation methods.

requirements.requirement_text: The Director may waive the requirement of (a)(1)(vi) for a site-specific evaluation of the designed manure storage structure and instead authorize a CAFO to use a technical evaluation developed for a class of specific facilities within a specified geographical area.
requirements.plain_language_summary: The Director can allow your CAFO to skip the individual site evaluation (from (a)(1)(vi)) if they approve a technical evaluation that covers a group of similar farms in your area.

requirements.requirement_text: Waste management and storage facilities designed, constructed, operated, and maintained consistent with the analysis conducted in paragraphs (a)(1)(i) through (a)(1)(vii) of this section and operated in accordance with the additional measures and records required by Sec. 412.47(a) and (b), will fulfill the requirements of this section.
requirements.plain_language_summary: Your waste management and storage facilities will meet the 'no discharge' rules if they are designed, built, run, and maintained according to the technical evaluation (from (a)(1)(i) through (a)(1)(vii)) and you follow the extra measures and record-keeping rules in section 412.47(a) and (b).

requirements.requirement_text: The Director has the discretion to request additional information to support a request for effluent limitations based on a site-specific open surface manure storage structure.
requirements.plain_language_summary: The Director can ask for more information if you request specific discharge limits for your open manure storage structure based on a site-specific evaluation.

requirements.requirement_text: Any source subject to this subpart that commenced discharging after April 14, 1993, and prior to April 14, 2003, which was a new source subject to the standards specified in Sec. 412.15, revised as of July 1, 2002, must continue to achieve those standards for the applicable time period specified in 40 CFR 122.29(d)(1). Thereafter, the source must achieve the standards specified in Sec. 412.43(a) and (b).
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your CAFO started discharging between April 14, 1993, and April 14, 2003, and was considered a new source under the old rules (section 412.15 from July 1, 2002), you must keep meeting those old standards for the time period in 40 CFR 122.29(d)(1). After that, you must meet the standards in section 412.43(a) and (b).
requirements.deadline: Continue to achieve standards for applicable time period in 40 CFR 122.29(d)(1); thereafter, achieve standards in 40 CFR 412.43(a) and (b).

requirements.requirement_text: Any source subject to this subpart that commenced discharging after April 14, 2003, and prior to January 20, 2009, which was a new source subject to the standards specified in Sec. 412.46(a) through (d) in the July 1, 2008, edition of 40 CFR part 439, must continue to achieve those standards for the applicable time period specified in 40 CFR 122.29(d)(1).
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your CAFO started discharging between April 14, 2003, and January 20, 2009, and was considered a new source under the rules in 40 CFR 412.46(a) through (d) (from the July 1, 2008 edition), you must keep meeting those standards for the time period specified in 40 CFR 122.29(d)(1).
requirements.deadline: Continue to achieve standards for applicable time period in 40 CFR 122.29(d)(1).

gaps: The facility's current NPDES general permit expiration date and whether a renewal application has been submitted 180 days prior to expiration are unknown (REQ-016).

While not legally enforceable in NC due to the November 2025 NC Supreme Court ruling, Calvin L. Rouse Farm is not required to submit annual reports detailing actual crop yields, nutrient content, application amounts, and soil/manure phosphorus test results as outlined in 40 CFR 122.42(e)(4)(viii) (REQ-048).

It is not confirmed which nutrient application rate approach (linear or narrative) Calvin L. Rouse Farm uses in its NMP, nor is there confirmation that annual calculations, manure/wastewater testing, and (if applicable) soil testing are performed as required by the chosen approach (REQ-051, REQ-054).
There is no confirmation that Calvin L. Rouse Farm submits updated versions of its Nutrient Management Plan to the Director, clearly identifying all changes, whenever revisions occur (REQ-055).

There is no confirmation that Calvin L. Rouse Farm's open surface liquid impoundments (lagoons) have a clearly visible depth marker indicating the minimum capacity necessary to contain the design storm runoff and precipitation (REQ-064).

It is unclear if Calvin L. Rouse Farm is classified as a "new source" CAFO under 40 CFR Part 412. If it is, there is no confirmation that its open surface manure storage structures have undergone or are designed to undergo the required site-specific technical evaluation to ensure no discharge (REQ-065, REQ-066, REQ-067, REQ-068, REQ-069, REQ-070, REQ-071, REQ-073).

The facility's operational history (commencement of discharge dates and "new source" status under specific historical regulations) is unknown, making it unclear if it is subject to the specific effluent standards outlined in 40 CFR 412.46(d) or (e) (REQ-075, REQ-076).
recommended_actions: Calvin L. Rouse Farm must confirm its NPDES general permit expiration date and ensure a renewal application is submitted to the Director at least 180 days before that date (REQ-016).

Although not legally mandated due to the NC Supreme Court ruling, Calvin L. Rouse Farm should consider voluntarily maintaining detailed records of actual crop yields, nutrient content of manure/wastewater, application rates, and soil/manure phosphorus test results. This practice supports sound nutrient management, demonstrates environmental stewardship, and provides robust documentation for potential liability protection (REQ-048).

Calvin L. Rouse Farm must identify whether its NMP uses the linear (40 CFR 122.42(e)(5)(i)) or narrative (40 CFR 122.42(e)(5)(ii)) rate approach. For the chosen approach, ensure annual calculations of maximum application rates are performed using the most recent representative manure/wastewater tests (within 12 months of application) and, if using the narrative approach, field-specific soil tests (REQ-051, REQ-054).

Calvin L. Rouse Farm must establish a procedure to submit the most current version of its Nutrient Management Plan to the Director, highlighting all changes from the previous version, whenever the plan is revised (REQ-055).

Calvin L. Rouse Farm must inspect all open surface liquid impoundments to verify the presence of a clearly visible depth marker that accurately indicates the minimum required capacity for the design storm, as per 40 CFR 412.37(a)(2) (REQ-064).

Calvin L. Rouse Farm should determine its "new source" status under 40 CFR Part 412. If classified as a new source, ensure that the open surface manure storage structures have undergone or are designed to undergo the required technical evaluation, including all specified elements (e.g., AWM software, climate data, SPAW Hydrology Tool), to establish "no discharge" effluent limitations (REQ-065, REQ-066, REQ-067, REQ-068, REQ-069, REQ-070, REQ-071, REQ-073).

Calvin L. Rouse Farm must review its operational history, including the date it commenced discharging and any prior "new source" classifications, to confirm whether it is subject to the specific effluent standards and compliance periods outlined in 40 CFR 412.46(d) or (e) (REQ-075, REQ-076).
summary: Calvin L. Rouse Farm, a Large Swine CAFO with a general NPDES permit, appears generally compliant with federal permitting requirements. However, several areas require verification, including permit renewal status, NMP update procedures, and the presence of required depth markers on impoundments. While annual reporting and phosphorus testing requirements were struck down by the NC Supreme Court, voluntary compliance is advisable for robust environmental management and liability protection.
